turns.reply:
I fixed `Segment.split_cells` in `rich/segment.py` so it no longer returns a left part wider than the cut when the text contains zero-width or combining characters. The patch is submitted (one file, 480 bytes).

The cause was in `_split_cells`: its proportional estimate for the split position could land past the cut when the prefix was already wider than the requested cell count. The forward scan then never walked back. I added a loop that rewinds the position while the prefix is wider than the cut.

I checked the fix with an exhaustive brute-force run over short strings mixing ASCII, wide CJK, emoji, combining marks and zero-width spaces. Before the fix there were 256 width violations; after it there are none. `tests/test_segment.py` passes (52 tests). I did not add a regression test, and I did not check the exact Textual scenario from the linked issue.
